(3) Value is being commoditized and colonized by EHR incumbents faster than any other agent category (Epic 'Art' Feb 2026 at ~42% acute-care, Microsoft Dragon, athenaAmbient, Oracle, Meditech) — the standalone winners' moat is a 2–3yr lead, not durable. So: a production-proven Expansion market with real wellbeing ROI, but a weak labor-DISPLACEMENT thesis and a rapidly closing value-capture window.

name: Agent Evaluation, Red-Team & Safety Testing
labor_tam: $4–9B [W] net-new (refined up from frozen $3–8B on EU-enforcement live + comp inflation; Medium confidence — comp anchors solid, headcount the binding uncertainty)

The open door is the ADJACENT white-space where the regulatory-independence mandate bites and generic tools don't fit: (1) regulated-vertical eval (healthcare/finance/legal agent testing); (2) continuous POST-deployment production eval/monitoring (as Art. 55 forces ongoing, not just pre-release, testing); (3) the expert red-teamer SUPPLY marketplace feeding Arena-style crowdsourcing. Underwrite the structural conflict-of-interest moat (a GPAI provider cannot self-certify its own safety) that neither model labs nor security incumbents can fill by definition.

If neither holds by that date — EU enforcement deferred/toothless (GPAI code-of-practice softening) and labs internalize eval so third-party citations drop → BEAR: L→5 (lab-captured), the category collapses into incumbents/OSS, standalone eval loses its protected niche.
anti: Consensus holds two opposing-but-both-wrong views: bulls fund eval as a hot startup category (aggregators claim it took ~35% of AI-safety capital), bears treat safety as a cost center that self-solves as models get safer. Both miss the durable truth — this track is the ANTI-C1 HEDGE: verification/eval demand is structurally COUNTER-CYCLICAL to the agent thesis. The wider the revenue-vs-delivered-value gap stays (METR −4% CI[−15,+9]; realized capture 0.1–11%), the MORE eval labor is needed — so W8.3 pays off precisely when the rest of the map disappoints. Second contrarian point: capital is misallocated — it floods the TOOLING layer (which OSS-deflates via PyRIT/Garak and gets incumbent-acquired), while the durable value is the net-new LABOR plus the regulatory-independence requirement that CANNOT be automated away or self-certified. The non-obvious moat is a structural conflict-of-interest (you can't grade your own safety), not a data/tech moat — which is why labs pay third parties despite building eval in-house.

It exists to close the exact model value-gaps that, once closed, reduce the need for it — and RL-environments + synthetic data already auto-handle ~80% of volume. The bull thesis ("largest net-new AI labor market") and the bear thesis ("transient RLHF crutch the models will obsolete") are the SAME fact viewed twice. Also: Scale — the incumbent that "won" — was kneecapped not by a rival but by its own lab investor (Meta), because any lab-owned vendor loses every other lab; NEUTRALITY is the moat and it structurally caps consolidation.
